name: ADM2483BRWZ-REEL
title: ADM2483: half-duplex RS-485 transceiver with iCoupler galvanic isolation, 500 kbps, 16-lead wide SOIC
summary: A half-duplex RS-485/RS-422 transceiver with a three-channel magnetic (iCoupler) isolator built in, so the logic pins and the bus pins sit on separate grounds. The logic side runs from 2.7 V to 5.5 V (VDD1) and the bus side from 5 V (VDD2, 4.75 V to 5.25 V). The driver is slew-limited, which caps the data rate at 500 kbps; the receiver input resistance of at least 96 kΩ lets 256 nodes share one bus, and its threshold sits between -200 mV and -30 mV so an open, shorted or idle line reads high. The barrier is rated 2500 V rms for one minute (UL 1577) with VIORM = 560 V peak, and the driver is protected by a current limit and a thermal cutout.

circuits.title: Driving PV with ADM809Z
circuits.description: A supervisor holds the power-valid pin low while VDD1 ramps. The ADM809Z sits on VDD1 with the ADM2483 and its active-low reset output drives PV directly. Its 2.32 V trip point lies above the 2.0 V that PV must wait for, so on the way up PV goes high one reset timeout (tPOR) after VDD1 passes 2.32 V, and on the way down PV falls as VDD1 drops through 2.32 V, before it reaches 2.0 V.

circuits.title: Isolated power supply circuit
circuits.description: A discrete push-pull converter makes the isolated 5 V for VDD2 from the logic supply VCC. One 74HC14 Schmitt inverter with 3.9 kΩ from output to input and 1 nF from input to ground oscillates at about 364 kHz. A 74HC74A D flip-flop, clocked by it with D tied to its Q-bar output, gives complementary square waves on Q and Q-bar, 180° apart, which switch two BS107A n-channel MOSFETs. Each MOSFET pulls one end of the 78253 transformer's primary to ground while the centre tap sits at VCC. On the far side of the barrier two SD103C Schottky diodes rectify the centre-tapped secondary into a 22 µF reservoir, and an ADP667 linear regulator, with SET and SHDN tied to the isolated ground, delivers 5 V to VDD2. VCC also feeds VDD1. 100 nF caps bypass the two logic chips.

parts.note: one Schmitt-trigger inverter of the six

circuits.title: Driver voltage measurement (VOD, VOC)
circuits.description: The driver outputs are loaded by two equal resistors R in series, A to B. VOD is read across the pair and VOC from their midpoint to ground; R is 50 Ω for the RS-422 case and 27 Ω for RS-485, or left open.

circuits.title: Driver voltage measurement with common-mode source (VOD3)
circuits.description: A 60 Ω resistor across A and B carries the differential load, and a 375 Ω resistor from each output meets at a source VTEST, swept from −7 V to +12 V against ground. VOD3 is read across the 60 Ω.

circuits.title: Driver propagation delay
circuits.description: RLDIFF (54 Ω) sits across A and B, and CL1 and CL2 (100 pF each) run from A and from B to a grounded midpoint. TxD is driven and the outputs timed.

circuits.title: Driver enable/disable
circuits.description: TxD is held at 0 V or 3 V and DE is pulsed. S1 picks output A or B; the chosen output carries CL to ground and RL to S2, which returns RL to VCC or to ground. VOUT is taken at the output.

parts.note: 100 pF for enable, 15 pF for disable

circuits.title: Receiver propagation delay
circuits.description: A and B are driven differentially with RE grounded, and RxD carries only CL (15 pF) to ground.

circuits.title: Receiver enable/disable
circuits.description: S1 puts +1.5 V or −1.5 V on A with B grounded, setting RxD high or low, and RE is pulsed. RxD carries CL to ground and RL to S2, which returns RL to VCC or to ground.

operation.text: The isolation is on the logic side. TxD and DE, referred to GND1, are encoded, sent across chip-scale transformers and decoded on the transceiver die, referred to GND2; the receiver output comes back the same way to RxD. The three channels are coreless, so a steady magnetic field cannot saturate them.

Driver and receiver share the A and B pins as one differential port. DE high enables the driver; RE low turns the receiver on; RE high puts RxD in high impedance. With the driver off, or with VDD1 or VDD2 at 0 V, A and B present only a light load. The driver's slew limit cuts reflections on badly terminated lines and limits signalling to 500 kbps. Receiver input impedance of 96 kΩ allows up to 256 transceivers on a bus.

The receiver threshold lies between −200 mV and −30 mV rather than straddling zero. With the inputs open or shorted, or with an idle terminated line whose differential voltage has decayed to 0 V, RxD is guaranteed high, so no external bias resistors on A and B are needed.
A current limit and a thermal cutout cover output shorts and bus contention. The driver outputs turn off at a die temperature of 150 °C and turn back on once it has cooled to 140 °C.

A, B and RxD reach their proper states once both supplies are above their power-up thresholds (VDD1 2.0 V, VDD2 3.3 V) and hold them until either supply drops under its power-down level (VDD1 1.0 V, VDD2 2.4 V). After VDD1 crosses its power-down threshold the outputs settle to their unpowered states within 4 µs.

PV keeps A and B from chattering when VDD1 ramps slowly (slower than 100 µs/V). Hold PV low until VDD1 is above 2.0 V, then drive it high; on power-down drive it low before VDD1 falls to 2.0 V. A reset supervisor such as the ADM809Z, threshold 2.32 V, can drive it (circuit pv-reset).

VDD2 to GND2 needs an isolated 5 V able to deliver 100 mA. Without an integrated isolated supply, a discrete push-pull converter serves (circuit isolated-supply): a centre-tapped transformer driven by two antiphase square waves, Schottky rectification and smoothing on the secondary, and an ADP667 linear regulator. An oscillator built from a Schmitt inverter with 3.9 kΩ and 1 nF runs at 364 kHz.

An alternating field can only cause an error by inducing enough voltage in a receiving coil to flip the decoder wrongly; the 3 V logic supply case is the most sensitive. At 1 MHz the allowed 0.2 kgauss induces 0.25 V, about half the 0.5 V sensing threshold; at worst polarity during a pulse it shrinks a received pulse of over 1.0 V to 0.75 V, still well above that threshold. The same limits, expressed as current in a conductor 5 mm, 100 mm or 1 m away, give the maximum allowable current curves. Strong high-frequency fields can also induce errors in loops formed by board traces feeding the following circuitry, so such traces need care in layout.
